subproblems.title: Differentiation of the radial cutoff mass under the integral sign (step 5)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N (Borel σ-algebra) and y ∈ ℝ^N. Let h : ℝ^N → ℝ be continuous, and let φ : ℝ → ℝ be of class C¹ with φ(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A², where A > 0. Let R ∈ ℝ with μ(B_R(y)) < ∞, where B_R(y) = closedBall y R. Then for every t₀ > 0 with t₀·A < R, the function t ↦ ∫ φ(|z − y|²/t²)·h(z) dμ(z) (Bochner integral) has derivative ∫ φ'(|z − y|²/t₀²)·(−2|z − y|²/t₀³)·h(z) dμ(z) at t₀, where φ' := deriv φ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (y : Euclidean N) (h : Euclidean N → ℝ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (A R t₀ : ℝ), Continuous h → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → 0 < A → (∀ s, A ^ 2 ≤ s → φ s = 0) → μ (closedBall y R) ≠ ∞ → 0 < t₀ → t₀ * A < R → HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ ↦ ∫ z, φ (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) * h z ∂μ) (∫ z, deriv φ (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t₀ ^ 2) * (-2 * ‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t₀ ^ 3) * h z ∂μ) t₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (differentiation under the integral sign in Simon 8.3.5), for an arbitrary measure μ that is finite on B_R(y) and an arbitrary continuous weight h.
Notation. B_r(y) := closedBall y r. For z ∈ ℝ^N put w := z − y and φ' := deriv φ. For t ∈ ℝ and z ∈ ℝ^N:
  F(t,z) := φ(‖w‖²/t²)·h(z),  F'(t,z) := φ'(‖w‖²/t²)·(−2‖w‖²/t³)·h(z).
K := B_R(y).

1. Constants. Since t₀ > 0 and A > 0, R > t₀A > 0, so t₀ < R/A. Put a := t₀/2 and b := (t₀ + R/A)/2. Then 0 < a < t₀ < b and bA < R. K is compact (a closed ball in ℝ^N) and measurable, and μ(K) < ∞ by hypothesis.

2. Cut-off facts.
 (i) If s > A², then φ vanishes on the open neighbourhood (A², ∞) of s, so φ'(s) = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq).
 (ii) If t ∈ [a, b] and z ∉ K, then ‖w‖ > R > bA ≥ tA > 0. Hence ‖w‖² > (tA)², i.e. ‖w‖²/t² > A². So φ(‖w‖²/t²) = 0 and, by (i), φ'(‖w‖²/t²) = 0. Thus F(t,z) = F'(t,z) = 0.

3. Continuity. φ and φ' are continuous (φ is C¹), and h is continuous. So for every t > 0 (in particular every t ∈ [a, b]) the maps z ↦ F(t,z) and z ↦ F'(t,z) are continuous, hence strongly measurable. Moreover (t,z) ↦ F'(t,z) is continuous on [a, b] × K, because t ≥ a > 0 there, so no division by zero occurs.

4. Domination. [a, b] × K is compact, so there is C ≥ 0 with |F'(t,z)| ≤ C for all (t,z) ∈ [a, b] × K. Explicitly one may take C := L·(2R²/a³)·H, where L bounds |φ'| on [0, R²/a²] and H bounds |h| on K: for (t,z) ∈ [a,b] × K, ‖w‖ ≤ R and t ≥ a, so ‖w‖²/t² ∈ [0, R²/a²] and 2‖w‖²/t³ ≤ 2R²/a³. Put bound(z) := C·1_K(z). By 2(ii), |F'(t,z)| ≤ bound(z) for all z and all t ∈ (a, b). bound is μ-integrable, since ∫ bound dμ = C·μ(K) < ∞.

5. Integrability of F(t₀,·). F(t₀,·) is continuous, hence bounded on the compact set K by some C₀. Since μ(K) < ∞, it is integrable on K (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). By 2(ii), with t₀ ∈ [a, b], it vanishes outside K. Hence it is μ-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).

6. Pointwise derivative. Fix z and let t ≠ 0. By the quotient rule, s(t) := ‖w‖²/t² has derivative −2‖w‖²/t³ at t. φ is differentiable, so by the chain rule t ↦ φ(s(t)) has derivative φ'(s(t))·(−2‖w‖²/t³). Multiplying by the constant h(z), t ↦ F(t,z) has derivative F'(t,z) at every t ∈ (a, b).

7. Conclusion. (a, b) is a neighbourhood of t₀. Apply differentiation under the integral sign (Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le with s := (a, b)). Its hypotheses hold:
 - F(t,·) is a.e.-strongly measurable for every t in the neighbourhood (a, b) of t₀ (step 3);
 - F(t₀,·) is integrable (step 5);
 - F'(t₀,·) is a.e.-strongly measurable (step 3);
 - ‖F'(t,z)‖ ≤ bound(z) for all z and t ∈ (a, b), and bound is integrable (step 4);
 - t ↦ F(t,z) has derivative F'(t,z) for all z and t ∈ (a, b) (step 6).
 So t ↦ ∫ F(t,z) dμ(z) has derivative ∫ F'(t₀,z) dμ(z) at t₀. That is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: a := t₀/2 and b := (t₀ + R/A)/2 give 0 < a < t₀ < b and bA < R; K := B_R(y) is compact with μ(K) < ∞
φ' = 0 on (A², ∞); for t ∈ [a,b] and z ∉ K, ‖z−y‖²/t² > A², so F(t,z) = F'(t,z) = 0
F' is continuous on [a,b] × K, hence bounded by some C; bound := C·1_K is μ-integrable
F(t₀,·) is continuous, bounded on K and zero off K, hence integrable
∂_t F(t,z) = φ'(‖z−y‖²/t²)(−2‖z−y‖²/t³)h(z) by the quotient and chain rules

subproblems.title: Weighted radial first-variation inequality at a fixed radius (corrected Simon 8.3.5; steps 1, 3, 4, 6)
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, W an n-varifold on U and y ∈ ℝ^N. Let h : ℝ^N → ℝ be of class C¹ with h ≥ 0. Let φ : ℝ → ℝ be of class C¹ and non-increasing with φ(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A², where A > 0. Let t > 0 with B_{tA}(y) = closedBall y (tA) ⊆ U. Assume (Div): for every a : ℝ^N → ℝ, c, z ∈ ℝ^N and S ∈ G(N,n) with a differentiable at z, div_S(w ↦ a(w)(w − c))(z) = n·a(z) + Da(z)[p_S(z − c)]. Here div_S = Varifold.tangentialDivergence and p_S = Grassmannian.project S; (Div) is the statement of the parent's dependency radial_field_divergence for these N, n. Let X_t(z) := h(z)φ(|z − y|²/t²)(z − y), and define the Bochner integrals Ĩ(t) := ∫ φ(|z − y|²/t²)h(z) dμ_W(z), J(t) := ∫ φ'(|z − y|²/t²)·(−2|z − y|²/t³)·h(z) dμ_W(z) with φ' := deriv φ, and G(t) := ∫ φ(|z − y|²/t²)·Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)] dW(z,S). Here μ_W = W.weight and dW = W.measure. Then n·Ĩ(t) − t·J(t) + G(t) ≤ δW(X_t), where δW = W.firstVariation.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (W : Varifold N n U) (y : Euclidean N) (h : Euclidean N → ℝ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (A t : ℝ), (∀ (a : Euclidean N → ℝ) (c z : Euclidean N) (S : Grassmannian N n), DifferentiableAt ℝ a z → Varifold.tangentialDivergence (fun w ↦ a w • (w - c)) z S = n * a z + fderiv ℝ a z (Grassmannian.project S (z - c))) → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → (∀ z, 0 ≤ h z) → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → Antitone φ → 0 < A → (∀ s, A ^ 2 ≤ s → φ s = 0) → 0 < t → closedBall y (t * A) ⊆ U → (n : ℝ) * (∫ z, φ (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) * h z ∂W.weight) - t * (∫ z, deriv φ (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) * (-2 * ‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 3) * h z ∂W.weight) + (∫ p, φ (‖p.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) * fderiv ℝ h p.1 (Grassmannian.project p.2 (p.1 - y)) ∂W.measure) ≤ W.firstVariation (fun z ↦ (h z * φ (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2)) • (z - y))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 3, 4 and 6 of the parent proof, at one fixed radius t, with the nonnegative normal term Q(t) dropped. This is Simon 8.3.5 with the sign of δV(X) corrected (erratum E2: the coefficient of δV(X) is '−'; see SimonGMT Chapter08/WeightedRadialIdentity.lean). The divergence of the radial field comes from hypothesis (Div), the exact statement of the parent's dependency radial_field_divergence.
Notation. w := z − y; s(z) := ‖w‖²/t²; φ' := deriv φ; a(z) := h(z)·φ(s(z)), so X_t(z) = a(z)(z − y). Also p_S := Grassmannian.project S and Dh := fderiv ℝ h. K := B_{tA}(y) = closedBall y (tA) is compact, and K ⊆ U by hypothesis. G := Grassmannian N n is a compact space.

1. Sign and support of φ and φ'. φ is non-increasing, so φ'(s) ≤ 0 for all s (Antitone.deriv_nonpos). If s > A², then φ vanishes on the open neighbourhood (A², ∞) of s, so φ'(s) = 0. If ‖w‖ ≥ tA, then ‖w‖²/t² ≥ A² (as t, A > 0), so φ(s(z)) = 0. If ‖w‖ > tA, then s(z) > A², so also φ'(s(z)) = 0. In particular, φ(s(z)) = φ'(s(z)) = 0 whenever z ∉ K.

2. Regularity of a and X_t. z ↦ ‖z − y‖² is C^∞ with derivative v ↦ 2⟨w, v⟩. So s is C¹ with Ds(z)[v] = (2/t²)⟨w, v⟩. Since φ and h are C¹, a = h·(φ∘s) is C¹. By the product and chain rules, for all z and v:
  Da(z)[v] = h(z)·φ'(s(z))·(2/t²)⟨w, v⟩ + φ(s(z))·Dh(z)[v].
 X_t, the product of a C¹ scalar function with the C¹ field z ↦ z − y, is C¹.

3. Support of X_t. If X_t(z) ≠ 0, then φ(s(z)) ≠ 0, so ‖w‖ < tA by step 1, i.e. z ∈ K. So support(X_t) ⊆ K. As K is closed, tsupport X_t ⊆ K ⊆ U, and as K is compact, X_t has compact support.

4. Pointwise divergence. Fix (z, S) and write s := s(z). The map w ↦ a(w)(w − y) is X_t, and a is differentiable at z (step 2). So (Div) with c := y gives
  div_S X_t(z) = n·a(z) + Da(z)[p_S w]
       = n·h(z)φ(s) + h(z)φ'(s)·(2/t²)⟨w, p_S w⟩ + φ(s)·Dh(z)[p_S w].

5. Projection facts. p_S is the linear map with matrix S.1. It is symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (Grassmannian.project_project). Hence ⟨w, p_S w⟩ = ⟨w, p_S(p_S w)⟩ = ⟨p_S w, p_S w⟩ = ‖p_S w‖². By Cauchy–Schwarz, ‖p_S w‖² = ⟨w, p_S w⟩ ≤ ‖w‖·‖p_S w‖, so ‖p_S w‖ ≤ ‖w‖. Hence ⟨w, p_S w⟩ ≤ ‖w‖².

6. Pointwise inequality. For (z,S) ∈ ℝ^N × G define
  E(z,S) := n·(φ(s)h(z)) − t·(φ'(s)·(−2‖w‖²/t³)·h(z)) + φ(s)·Dh(z)[p_S w].
 Since t·(−2‖w‖²/t³) = −2‖w‖²/t², step 4 gives
  div_S X_t(z) − E(z,S) = (2/t²)·h(z)·(−φ'(s))·(‖w‖² − ⟨w, p_S w⟩) ≥ 0,
 because h(z) ≥ 0, −φ'(s) ≥ 0 (step 1) and ‖w‖² − ⟨w, p_S w⟩ ≥ 0 (step 5). So E ≤ div_S X_t pointwise.

7. Integrability with respect to W.measure on ℝ^N × G.
 (a) (z,S) ↦ div_S X_t(z) is integrable by Varifold.integrable_tangentialDivergence: X_t is C¹ with compact support and tsupport X_t ⊆ U (steps 2–3).
 (b) Put f₁(z,S) := φ(s(z))h(z), f₂(z,S) := φ'(s(z))·(−2‖w‖²/t³)·h(z) and f₃(z,S) := φ(s(z))·Dh(z)[p_S w]. They are continuous on ℝ^N × G: φ, φ', h and Dh are continuous (φ and h are C¹). Also (S, v) ↦ p_S v is continuous, because its i-th coordinate is Σ_j S.1_{ij}·v_j (LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr), a polynomial in the entries of S.1 and v.
 (c) By step 1 each f_i vanishes outside K × G. K × G is compact (G is compact), so each f_i is bounded on it. W.measure(K × G) < ∞ (Varifold.finite_on_compact: K is compact and K ⊆ U). Hence f₁, f₂, f₃ are integrable, and so is E = n·f₁ − t·f₂ + f₃.

8. Integration. δW(X) = ∫ div_S X(z) dW(z,S) by definition (Varifold.firstVariation). By linearity (integral_add, integral_sub, integral_const_mul) and monotonicity (integral_mono, using steps 6–7):
  n∫f₁ dW − t∫f₂ dW + ∫f₃ dW = ∫E dW ≤ ∫ div_S X_t(z) dW(z,S) = δW(X_t).

9. Identification. μ_W = W.weight is the push-forward of W.measure under (z,S) ↦ z. So for continuous g : ℝ^N → ℝ, ∫ g dμ_W = ∫ g(z) dW(z,S) (integral_map). With g(z) = φ(s(z))h(z) this gives ∫f₁ dW = Ĩ(t). With g(z) = φ'(s(z))(−2‖w‖²/t³)h(z) it gives ∫f₂ dW = J(t). And ∫f₃ dW = G(t) by definition. Therefore n·Ĩ(t) − t·J(t) + G(t) ≤ δW(X_t). ∎
proof_key_steps: φ' ≤ 0; φ(s(z)) = 0 if ‖z−y‖ ≥ tA, and φ'(s(z)) = 0 if ‖z−y‖ > tA
a = h·φ(‖·−y‖²/t²) is C¹ with Da(z)[v] = hφ'(s)(2/t²)⟨w,v⟩ + φ(s)Dh(z)[v]; X_t is C¹ with tsupport in B_{tA}(y) ⊆ U
(Div) gives div_S X_t = n·a + Da[p_S w]; p_S symmetric and idempotent gives ⟨w, p_S w⟩ = ‖p_S w‖² ≤ ‖w‖²
div_S X_t − E = (2/t²)h(−φ')(‖w‖² − ⟨w, p_S w⟩) ≥ 0 pointwise
the integrands are continuous, vanish off B_{tA}(y) × G and have finite mass there, so they are integrable; div_S X_t is integrable
integral_mono, linearity and μ_W = π_# W give nĨ(t) − tJ(t) + G(t) ≤ δW(X_t)

subproblems.title: Tilt-excess bound for the gradient term G(t) (step 7(b))
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, W an n-varifold on U, P ∈ G(N,n) and y ∈ ℝ^N. Let ε ≥ 0, M ≥ 0, A > 0 and t > 0. Let h : ℝ^N → ℝ be any function, and φ : ℝ → [0,1] with φ(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A². Write t_P(S) for the operator norm of p_S − p_P, i.e. ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P)‖, and Dh := fderiv ℝ h. Assume (2'): ∫⁻_{B_{tA}(y)×G(N,n)} ofReal(t_P(S)) dW(z,S) ≤ ofReal(ε(tA)^n) in [0,∞] (an extended-real Lebesgue integral), where B_{tA}(y) = closedBall y (tA). Assume (grad): |Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)]| ≤ M·t_P(S)·|z − y| for all z ∈ ℝ^N and S ∈ G(N,n). Then |G(t)| ≤ M·A^{n+1}·ε·t^{n+1}, where G(t) := ∫ φ(|z − y|²/t²)·Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)] dW(z,S) is a Bochner integral.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (W : Varifold N n U) (P : Grassmannian N n) (y : Euclidean N) (ε M A t : ℝ) (h : Euclidean N → ℝ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → 0 ≤ M → 0 < A → 0 < t → (∫⁻ z in closedBall y (t * A) ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), ENNReal.ofReal ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap z.2 - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ ∂W.measure) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ε * (t * A) ^ n) → (∀ (z : Euclidean N) (S : Grassmannian N n), |fderiv ℝ h z (Grassmannian.project S (z - y))| ≤ M * ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ * ‖z - y‖) → (∀ s, 0 ≤ φ s ∧ φ s ≤ 1) → (∀ s, A ^ 2 ≤ s → φ s = 0) → |∫ p, φ (‖p.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) * fderiv ℝ h p.1 (Grassmannian.project p.2 (p.1 - y)) ∂W.measure| ≤ M * A ^ (n + 1) * ε * t ^ (n + 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7(b) of the parent proof: the estimate of the gradient term by hypothesis (2r) at radius r = tA, stated for one radius.
Notation. w := z − y. t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P)‖ ≥ 0. g(z,S) := φ(‖w‖²/t²)·Dh(z)[p_S w], so G(t) = ∫ g dW. K := B_{tA}(y) × G(N,n) = closedBall y (tA) ×ˢ univ, a measurable set. Note tA > 0.

1. Pointwise bound.
 - Let (z,S) ∈ K, i.e. ‖w‖ ≤ tA. Since 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, |φ(‖w‖²/t²)| ≤ 1. By (grad), |g(z,S)| ≤ 1·M·t_P(S)·‖w‖ ≤ M·(tA)·t_P(S), using M ≥ 0 and t_P(S) ≥ 0.
 - Let (z,S) ∉ K, i.e. ‖w‖ > tA > 0. Then ‖w‖² > (tA)², so ‖w‖²/t² > A², hence φ(‖w‖²/t²) = 0 and g(z,S) = 0.
 So for all (z,S), in [0,∞]: ofReal|g(z,S)| ≤ 1_K(z,S)·ofReal(M·tA)·ofReal(t_P(S)). Here ofReal(xy) = ofReal(x)·ofReal(y) is used with x = M·tA ≥ 0.

2. Lebesgue integral bound. The lower Lebesgue integral is monotone for arbitrary functions (lintegral_mono). K is measurable, so the indicator can be turned into a set integral (lintegral_indicator). The finite constant ofReal(M·tA) can be pulled out (lintegral_const_mul'). Hence
  ∫⁻ ofReal|g| dW ≤ ∫⁻ 1_K·ofReal(M·tA)·ofReal(t_P(S)) dW(z,S)
           = ofReal(M·tA)·∫⁻_K ofReal(t_P(S)) dW(z,S)
           ≤ ofReal(M·tA)·ofReal(ε(tA)^n) = ofReal(M·tA·ε(tA)^n).
 The last inequality is hypothesis (2'); the last equality uses M·tA ≥ 0.

3. Bochner integral. For every function g, ‖∫ g dW‖ ≤ (∫⁻ ofReal‖g‖ dW).toReal (norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm). This needs no integrability: a non-integrable g has Bochner integral 0. toReal is monotone on finite values (ENNReal.toReal_mono), and M·tA·ε(tA)^n ≥ 0 because ε ≥ 0 and M ≥ 0. So
  |G(t)| = |∫ g dW| ≤ (ofReal(M·tA·ε(tA)^n)).toReal = M·tA·ε·(tA)^n = M·A^{n+1}·ε·t^{n+1}. ∎
proof_key_steps: on B_{tA}(y) × G, |g| ≤ M·tA·t_P(S) by (grad) and |φ| ≤ 1; off it, φ = 0, so g = 0
∫⁻ ofReal|g| dW ≤ ofReal(M tA)·∫⁻_{B_{tA}(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ ofReal(M·tA·ε(tA)^n), by (2')
|∫ g dW| ≤ (∫⁻ ofReal|g| dW).toReal ≤ M·tA·ε(tA)^n = M·A^{n+1}·ε·t^{n+1}
